frontier.hypothesis: F4'' - the 2-point rand() delay-slot residue (insns 50 and 54) is the ONLY remaining gap, and it is still the s3 tension: target's `move s0,zero` in the jal delay slot requires `i = 0;` to be emitted pre-call, and every pre-call placement costs the counter allocno $s0 (re-measured 8/8/8 on the floor-2 base). The untried surface is no longer WHERE `i = 0;` goes but WHAT ELSE can fill that delay slot, or how to make the counter allocno survive a pre-call init.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c:fill_simple_delay_slots fills a CALL_INSN's slot by BACKWARD search over preceding insns (the forward search is blocked here because the intervening andi/addiu both reference the call's $v0 result and it cannot cross the beqz). global.c:allocno_compare then decides $s0 by priority = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length*10000; a pre-call init puts the counter at ~6153 against h's 8750.
frontier.next_probe: Two cheap probes, in order. (1) Re-run the s3 instrumentation on the FLOOR-2 base - `bash tmp/grind/func_800174F4/s3/alloc.sh <tag>` and `findreg.sh <tag> <pseudo>` - to read the counter and `h` allocnos' CURRENT n_refs/live_length/priority. Cluster (A)'s new live range may have shifted h's numbers, and s3's inequality was measured on the floor-8 base; the arithmetic must be re-derived before any more structural guessing. (2) Attack the counter's n_refs rather than its live_length: the inequality needs counter n_refs >= 6 at live_length 13 (2*6/13 = 9230 > 8750). s3 killed sharing the counter with the case-20 D_800A37C0 counter (18/24), but that was on the floor-8 base where the case-20 region had a different allocno population; re-measure it on floor 2.

frontier.hypothesis: The `mode` second-def lever generalizes: other roles in this function that target keeps in one register may also want one C variable with several live ranges. In particular `prim` ($s2) and `env`/counter ($s0) are already single-variable, but the case-20 block still declares a2_val / a0_val / div_result / counter as four separate locals where target may be reusing registers.
frontier.mechanism: Same global.c:find_reg exclusion arithmetic that closed cluster (A): a second def of an existing pseudo extends its live range and changes which registers are excluded when it is allocated, without forcing it callee-save.
